text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-War in the West Bank and Gaza strip is a replay of Lebanon's civil war. Will the "new intifada" lead to a military operation against Lebanon.
-A diplomatic delegation headed by Foreign Minister Bouez to New York today. Lebanon is satisfied with the work of the five nation committee monitoring a ceasefire between Lebanon and Israel.
-President of the World Bank: We are eager to help Lebanon.
-Minister of Information warns banned television stations against broadcasting news of foreign televisions.

-Lebanon and Syria signed a judicial agreement, an extension to an earlier agreement. Syrian Minister of Justice Hassoun: We want the Lebanese citizen to feel that he is Syrian and the Syrian to feel he is Lebanese.
-Palestinians staged a strike and burned tyres in Lebanon's refugee camps.
-The UNESCO reopened its regional office in Beirut.
-Lebanon will ask Consultative Group for $5 billion.
-Head of Lebanon's Beirut Stock Exchange said a crosslisting agreement with Kuwait and Egypt will fulfill the dreams of Beirut markets.
